question_text: The room ____ every day.
explanation: Present simple passive uses am/is/are + past participle.

question_text: The window ____ yesterday.
explanation: Past simple passive uses was/were + past participle.

question_text: The report ____ tomorrow morning.
explanation: Future passive uses will be + past participle.

question_text: The song was written ____ a young composer.
explanation: Use by to mention the agent in a passive sentence.

question_text: Choose the passive form: They clean the office every night.

options.label: C
options.text: The office is clean every night.

options.label: D
options.text: The office is cleaned every night.

explanation: The object becomes the subject, then use is + cleaned.

question_text: These emails ____ automatically.
explanation: Plural subjects use are + past participle in the present passive.

question_text: The door ____ locked during the day.
explanation: Negative passive places not after the be verb: is not locked.

question_text: The form must ____ before Friday.
explanation: Modal passive uses modal + be + past participle.

question_text: The documents ____ already ____.
explanation: Present perfect passive uses have/has been + past participle.

question_text: Where ____ the keys kept?
explanation: Passive questions still use the correct be verb before the subject.

question_text: She ____ coffee every morning.
explanation: Use present simple for habits; third-person singular adds s.

question_text: Look! The children ____ in the garden.
explanation: Use present continuous for actions happening now.

question_text: I ____ my homework last night.
explanation: Use past simple with finished time expressions like last night.

question_text: They ____ here since 2020.
explanation: Use present perfect with since to connect past and present.

question_text: I ____ dinner when the phone rang.
explanation: Past continuous describes the longer action interrupted by a past simple action.

question_text: We ____ visit our grandparents this weekend.
explanation: Use be going to for planned future actions.

question_text: Have you ever ____ sushi?
explanation: Present perfect questions use have/has + past participle.

question_text: By the time we arrived, the movie ____.
explanation: Past perfect shows the action that happened before another past action.

question_text: I ____ this answer is correct.
explanation: Think meaning believe is usually used as a stative verb.

question_text: I think it ____ rain later.
explanation: Use will for predictions based on opinion.

question_text: The woman ____ lives next door is a doctor.
explanation: Use who for people in relative clauses.

question_text: This is the phone ____ I bought yesterday.
explanation: Use which for things.

question_text: This is the cafe ____ we met.
explanation: Use where to refer to a place.

question_text: The student ____ laptop was stolen called the police.
explanation: Use whose to show possession.

question_text: The book ____ you recommended was excellent.
explanation: That can refer to things in defining relative clauses.

question_text: The man ____ I saw at the station is my teacher.
explanation: Whom can be used for a person as the object of a relative clause.

question_text: Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: A
options.text: The girl who sits near me is kind.

options.label: B
options.text: The girl who near me sits is kind.

options.label: C
options.text: The girl sits who near me is kind.

options.label: D
options.text: The girl who is kind sits near me is.

explanation: A relative clause follows normal clause word order after the relative pronoun.

question_text: My brother, ____ lives in Canada, is visiting us.
explanation: Use who, not that, in a non-defining relative clause about a person.

question_text: Choose the sentence where the relative pronoun is correctly omitted.

options.label: A
options.text: The movie I watched was funny.

options.label: B
options.text: The man lives next door is friendly.

options.label: C
options.text: The city I live is busy.

options.label: D
options.text: The student won the prize is absent.

explanation: An object relative pronoun can be omitted, but a subject relative pronoun cannot.

question_text: I remember the day ____ we first met.
explanation: Use when to refer to a time.

question_text: If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it ____.
explanation: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for facts.

question_text: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
explanation: First conditional uses if + present simple, will + base verb.

question_text: If I had more time, I ____ a new language.
explanation: Second conditional uses if + past simple, would + base verb.

question_text: If she had studied harder, she ____ the exam.
explanation: Third conditional uses if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

question_text: You will miss the bus ____ you hurry.
explanation: Unless means if not.

question_text: If he ____ early, he will call us.
explanation: Do not use will in the if-clause of a first conditional.

question_text: If I had saved more money, I ____ a better car now.
explanation: This mixed conditional connects a past condition with a present result.

question_text: If I ____ you, I would apologize.
explanation: In formal second conditional, use were with all subjects.

question_text: Choose the sentence with the same meaning: If you do not study, you will fail.

options.label: A
options.text: Unless you study, you will fail.

options.label: B
options.text: Unless you do not study, you will fail.

options.label: C
options.text: If you study, you will fail.

options.label: D
options.text: Unless you study, you will pass.

explanation: Unless already means if not, so do not add another negative.

question_text: If they had left earlier, they would have ____ the train.
explanation: Would have is followed by a past participle.

question_text: Direct: She said, "I am tired." Reported: She said that she ____ tired.
explanation: In reported speech, present simple often backshifts to past simple.

question_text: Direct: Tom said, "I like my job." Reported: Tom said that ____ liked ____ job.
explanation: Pronouns change according to the speaker and context.

question_text: Direct: "Do you speak English?" He asked me ____ English.
explanation: Reported yes/no questions use if or whether and statement word order.

question_text: Direct: "Where do you live?" She asked me where ____.
explanation: Reported wh-questions use statement word order.

question_text: Direct: "Close the door," the teacher said. Reported: The teacher told me ____ the door.
explanation: Reported commands often use told + object + to-infinitive.

question_text: Direct: He said, "I will call you tomorrow." Reported: He said he would call me ____.
explanation: Tomorrow often changes to the next day in reported speech.

question_text: Direct: Anna said, "I can swim." Reported: Anna said that she ____ swim.
explanation: Can usually backshifts to could in reported speech.

question_text: She ____ me that she was busy.
explanation: Use told with an object: told me.

question_text: Direct: "Do not touch that," he said. Reported: He told me ____ that.
explanation: Negative reported commands use not + to-infinitive.

question_text: The teacher said that water ____ at 100 degrees Celsius.
explanation: Backshift is not necessary for general truths.

question_text: The meeting starts ____ 9 a.m.
explanation: Use at for exact times.

question_text: My birthday is ____ Monday.
explanation: Use on for days and dates.

question_text: They moved here ____ 2021.
explanation: Use in for years, months, and long periods.

question_text: She is waiting ____ the bus stop.
explanation: Use at for a specific point or location.

question_text: The keys are ____ my bag.
explanation: Use in when something is inside a container or space.

question_text: There is a picture ____ the wall.
explanation: Use on for something attached to a surface.

question_text: She is interested ____ learning Spanish.
explanation: The adjective interested is followed by in.

question_text: He is good ____ solving problems.
explanation: The adjective good is followed by at.

question_text: We are going ____ the airport.
explanation: Use to for movement toward a destination.

question_text: I slept ____ the flight.
explanation: Use during to say when something happens within an event.

question_text: Where do passengers usually check in for a flight?
explanation: A check-in counter is where passengers confirm their flight and luggage.

question_text: A boarding pass is used to ____.
explanation: A boarding pass shows that a passenger can board a flight.

question_text: A reservation means ____.
explanation: A reservation is an arrangement made in advance.

question_text: The hotel reception is the place where guests usually ____.
explanation: Guests check in at hotel reception.

question_text: A one-way ticket means you ____.

options.label: A
options.text: travel to a place without a return ticket

explanation: One-way means only one direction, not a return journey.

question_text: A round-trip ticket means ____.

options.label: A
options.text: a ticket for going and returning

options.label: B
options.text: a ticket for one bus stop

explanation: Round-trip means both the outward and return journey.

question_text: If your flight is delayed, it means the flight ____.
explanation: Delayed means later than the expected time.

question_text: Lost luggage means ____.
explanation: Luggage refers to bags; lost luggage means the bags are missing.

question_text: A passport is mainly used to ____.

options.label: A
options.text: prove your identity when traveling internationally

explanation: A passport is an official identity document for international travel.

question_text: A visa is ____.

options.label: A
options.text: official permission to enter or stay in a country

explanation: A visa gives permission to enter or stay in a country for a purpose.

question_text: The final episode should ____ after the recap.
explanation: Modal passive uses modal + be + past participle: should be watched.

question_text: Spoilers must ____ before the anime review is posted.
explanation: After must, passive voice needs be + past participle: must be hidden.

question_text: The character design can ____ after fan feedback.
explanation: Can be improved follows modal + be + past participle.

question_text: The animation schedule might ____ if the studio needs more time.
explanation: Might be delayed is modal passive: might + be + past participle.

question_text: The invitations ____ last week.
explanation: Plural past passive uses were + past participle.

question_text: When ____ the bridge built?
explanation: Past passive questions use was/were before the subject.

question_text: My brother usually ____ to school by bus.
explanation: Usually signals a habit, so use present simple with third-person singular -es.

question_text: She ____ just ____ the email.
explanation: Present perfect uses has/have + past participle.

question_text: I will call you when I ____ home.
explanation: Use present simple, not will, in future time clauses after when.

question_text: The movie ____ we watched last night was funny.
explanation: That can refer to things as the object of a defining relative clause.

question_text: My laptop, ____ I bought last year, still works well.
explanation: Use which, not that, in a non-defining relative clause about a thing.

question_text: The company ____ she works for is expanding.
explanation: That can introduce an object relative clause; the preposition for stays after the verb.

question_text: If you heat water to 100 degrees Celsius, it ____.
explanation: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for facts.

question_text: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
explanation: First conditional uses if + present simple, will + base verb.

question_text: If I had studied medicine, I ____ a doctor now.
explanation: This mixed conditional connects a past unreal condition with a present result.

question_text: Direct: "I am tired." Reported: She said that she ____ tired.
explanation: Present simple or continuous often backshifts to past in reported speech.

question_text: Direct: "Where do you live?" Reported: He asked me where I ____.
explanation: Reported questions use statement word order and usually backshift the tense.

question_text: Direct: "Please wait here." Reported: She asked me ____ there.
explanation: Reported requests use asked + object + to-infinitive.

question_text: Please submit the assignment ____ Friday.
explanation: By means no later than a deadline.

question_text: The bank is ____ the post office and the supermarket.
explanation: Between means in the middle of two people, places, or things.

question_text: Many children are afraid ____ the dark.
explanation: The adjective afraid is followed by of.

question_text: The cat jumped ____ the box.
explanation: Into shows movement from outside to inside a place.

question_text: The gate is the place where passengers ____.
explanation: At an airport gate, passengers wait and board their flight.

question_text: A double room is usually for ____.
explanation: A double room is designed for two people, often with one large bed.

question_text: Which item do you use to write on paper?
explanation: A pen is used for writing.

question_text: To wake up means to ____.
explanation: Wake up means to stop sleeping and become awake.

question_text: A deadline is ____.

options.label: A
options.text: the latest time something must be finished

explanation: A deadline is the final time or date by which work must be completed.

question_text: A classmate is ____.

options.label: A
options.text: a person in the same class as you

options.label: B
options.text: a person who drives a taxi

explanation: A classmate studies in the same class as you.

question_text: If someone is nervous, they feel ____.
explanation: Nervous means worried, anxious, or not relaxed.

question_text: To download a file means to ____.

options.label: A
options.text: copy it from the internet to your device

explanation: Download means to receive data from another system onto your device.
